query_aliases: best lens for birds in flight
profile_notes: Scoped to telephoto glass for living subjects in the field, NOT landscape. GATE: focal_length_mm >= 300. Reach is a SPEC (focal_length_mm, well-populated per task), not an axis, so the telephoto floor is enforced as a hard gate. Threshold rationale: research consensus puts the practical wildlife entry at 300mm, with ~400mm the ideal for most subjects and 500-600mm+ for small birds. 300 is chosen as the INCLUSIVE floor so versatile, widely-used wildlife zooms qualify (70-300, 100-400, 150-600, 200-500/200-600, and physical-300mm primes such as M4/3 300 f/4 which is 600mm-equivalent) while short-tele/portrait/standard glass (70-200, 24-70) is correctly excluded. A 400mm floor was rejected: it would drop popular 70-300/100-300 options and shrink the guide. NOTE: gate reads physical mm (not equivalent focal length) and, for zooms, is assumed to read the LONG/max end (its reach) -- see open question. NO max_aperture gate: fast glass helps (low light, subject isolation, AF), but hard-gating aperture would wrongly exclude the f/6.3 superzooms (150-600, 200-600) that are mainstream wildlife tools; aperture is therefore left ungated. WEIGHTS -- CRUX at 3: optical_performance (sharpness/resolving power at the long end and at distance is the defining lens quality for wildlife), af_performance (fast, decisive AF for erratic subjects and birds-in-flight). AT 2: handling (weight, balance, tripod-collar handling of long/heavy glass over long sessions), build (weather sealing / field durability). AT 1: chromatic_aberration (fringing on high-contrast edges like feathers against bright sky at long tele), bokeh (subject isolation from busy backgrounds -- nice, secondary), color_rendition. Deliberately UNWEIGHTED (0/omitted): af_noise (stills-irrelevant), distortion + vignetting + coma (negligible or irrelevant for wildlife tele), filter_thread. gear_class excludes novelty only. NATURE-SCOPE: same as the body profile -- 'nature' is a wildlife co-occurrence term; generic landscape/nature queries are excluded because they invert these needs. Ratified by Lee 2026-09-14.
